note: Proposed (not-shipped) contract shape per docs/design/design-pipeline.md §2 S4 and the design-topology-selection skill. Selection was KB-assisted via the shipped `klt kb` verb (docs/cli/kb.md).

kb_queries.cmd: klt kb search "single-stage transconductance amplifier" --format json

kb_queries.result: matched entry read in full (topology, sizing_approach, layout_idioms, pdk_portability)

rationale: The block spec (single-stage, unity-gain buffer, 30 dB / 5 MHz / 60 deg PM at ~40-60 uA on sky130, 1 pF load) matches the KB entry's spec_class verbatim ('general-purpose single-stage transconductance amplifier ... the baseline building block for feedback amplifiers ... in low-to-moderate gain, area- and power-constrained analog/mixed-signal PHY blocks'). The 5T OTA is the simplest topology that meets a low-to-moderate-gain buffer spec at minimum device count and power; folded-cascode (higher gain, more headroom cost) and two-stage Miller (higher gain, compensation complexity) both exceed what a 30 dB buffer needs. Chosen for spec fit, not familiarity.
matched_spec_fields: dc_open_loop_gain_db.min = 30 (KB: 'low-to-moderate gain', tens of dB at practical sky130 lengths)
closed_loop_config = unity-gain follower (KB: 'baseline building block for feedback amplifiers')
known_limitations: Single-ended DC gain is limited to ~one stage's gm*ro (tens of dB); the KB entry notes sky130 minimum-length devices have low intrinsic gain, so channel lengths well above minimum are required (reflected in S5 sizing: L=0.5-1 um on all devices). Recorded, not silently absorbed.
The KB corpus is shallow (design doc §4); a single matching entry is a strong fit here but the search space is not exhaustive. This match is corpus-confirmed, not merely model-knowledge.
